comment: Provisional. Ratios from 3 runs on 2026-11-16, load average 200 to 229 on a shared 512-core machine: keyed yuka/solid 1.058, 1.144 and 1.152 (the last from make bench-gate); ssr yuka-stream/solid-node 1.389, 1.603 and 1.368; LCP page/plain HTML 1.04 to 1.64; TBT 0 ms on every page. The server-reason-react limit is from bench/ssr/README.md (1.76 after ticket 31), since it is out of the build. max_js_raw is the exact raw bytes of JavaScript files and inline scripts of each page: change it with the change that changes the bytes. Set again on 5349ba5: pull requests 27, 28 and 30 grew / and /my to 200,388 B and /issue/YUK-1 to 170,568 B without a change here, and pull request 26 then moved the router code out of the start chunk. Raised by 830 B on each page for issue 11: the scheduler walks a chain of memos with a loop. Raised by 199 B on /, /my and /issue/YUK-1 for Action.start, the abort of a query Action.call when its owner is disposed, and a form answer that arrives after its form is gone. Raised by 141 B on /, /my and /issue/YUK-1 for the demo issue overlay: c21860e (close on a click outside, Close button in the page header) added 157 B without a change here, and 0dbb27d removed 16 B. SSR solid-node limit set to 1.0 (the v1 target, SSR faster than Solid) from 20 main CI runs on ubuntu-latest, 2026-11-16. The rounds of one run agree: per-round yuka-stream/solid-node ratios differ by 4.4% or less in a run. The runs do not: the ratio groups by runner, seen in the absolute req/s of solid-node. Solid near 3,800 to 4,250 req/s: 8 runs, 1.229 to 1.268. Near 5,250 to 5,550: 7 runs, 1.202 to 1.262. Near 6,700 to 7,000: 3 runs, 1.062, 1.104 and 1.122 (5ca0734, 6d21a08, 3f156ec; 6d21a08 changes only docs after f6a3ce7 at 1.252). Near 7,100 to 7,300: 2 runs, 1.283 and 1.313. Both servers use one thread, so the groups come from the runner CPU type; more or paired rounds do not change them (paired-round medians move each run by 0.025 or less). With 1.0 all 20 runs pass and the worst keeps a margin of 5.9%. The Yuka slowdown that fails a run is 5.9% to 10.8% on the slowest group and 16.8% to 23.9% on the others: replayed on the 20 runs, a 10% slowdown fails 2 and a 20% slowdown fails 11. A tighter limit needs a limit per CPU: run.ts records the CPU model in the result and the log, so collect it first. Raised for compiled-view step 1 (each child and attribute of an HTML tag that is not a constant is a hole): / and /my by 74 B, /issue/YUK-1 by 79 B. The bytes are calls of functions of other modules in the markup, which are now holes: the hrefs from Links, Theme.label and the Model.Issue labels. Raised by 5 B on / and /my and lowered by 4 B on /issue/YUK-1 for Remote.state and Live.state: each Remote.make and Live.make keeps a memo of the status with the optimistic changes applied, made in one helper of Optimistic for both. Raised by 88 B on /, /my and /issue/YUK-1 for the runtime part of the static-hole drop: an effect, hole or attribute hole whose first run reads no State is not kept by its owner, unless it adds a bubbling event handler, whose owner must be disposed with its parent. The JavaScript heap of /w/stress (2,000 rows) goes from 14.60 to 11.86 MB (11.16 MB before every non-constant JSX expression was a hole; 11.17 MB when a handler did not keep its owner). The server part (no markers for such a hole) was not kept: it cost 543 B more on / and /my, 487 B more on /issue/YUK-1 and 0.23 MB more heap on /w/stress, for 30 fewer comment nodes on /insights. Raised by 203 B on /, /my and /issue/YUK-1 for State.select: a read of a memo first updates a selector whose source changed, so a memo over is_selected is up to date in a batch. Raised by 801 B on / and /my for the shared Remote request: uses of one query with the same input share one request in flight, and a request is aborted only when its last use is disposed. Raised by 760 B on / and /my for cache tags: a Remote use with ?tags sends its query again when an action answer names one of its tags; /issue/YUK-1 goes down by 5 B (Platform.acted now gets the answer fields).
